land.text: Bit Adini on the Euphrates south of Carchemish

successors.note: Til Barsip was renamed Kar-Shulmanu-asharedu after Shalmaneser III (Tell Ahmar page).

capitals.name: Til Barsip (Tell Ahmar)
capitals.note: The Tell Ahmar page: "about 20 kilometers south of ancient Carchemish" on the Euphrates; the coordinates are my reading of that sentence (the page gives none).

correction.text: Bit Adini between the Balikh and the Euphrates, south of Carchemish

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -1000..-857: no Cliopatria shape. The page puts the state "between the Balikh and Euphrates rivers, usually thought to be in the bend of the Euphrates, south of Carchemish" and says it "extended westwards into northern Syria"; the territory included Masuwari (Til Barsip), Asmu, Dabigu, Dummetu, Kaprabu and La'la'ru (unlocated). Drawn as a 70 km circle at Til Barsip (my reading; no frontier on the pages).

region.text: Bit Adini on the middle Euphrates

ledger.note: c. 1000 BC: Bit Adini is established. The infobox gives "c. 1000 BC"; the page gives no founding event or founder and describes "an Aramaean state that existed as an independent kingdom" with its capital at Til Barsip (Tell Ahmar). The land is my reading.

region.text: Bit Adini on the middle Euphrates

ledger.note: 857/856 BC: Bit Adini falls to Shalmaneser III. "Ahuni of Bit Adini resisted for several years, but he surrendered to Shalmaneser in the winter of 857/856 BCE" (Neo-Assyrian Empire page); the Bit Adini page: "In 856-5 BC, the kingdom was conquered and absorbed into the" Assyrian Empire; the Tell Ahmar page: Til Barsip fell "in the 856 BC" and was renamed Kar-Shulmanu-asharedu. Mirrors the neo-assyrian-empire gain.

wars.name: Ahuni and the conquest of Bit Adini
wars.outcome: "Ahuni of Bit Adini resisted for several years, but he surrendered to Shalmaneser in the winter of 857/856 BCE."
wars.note: The Bit Adini page also has Ahuni in the 853 coalition at Qarqar, which does not fit its own end date.

certainty.note: No frontier on the pages: the state is a circle at its capital.

sources.title: Bit Adini
sources.note: Infobox c. 1000-856/5 BC; capital Til Barsip; Balikh-Euphrates bend south of Carchemish; Ahuni; Qarqar 853 (inconsistent); conquered 856-5.

sources.title: Neo-Assyrian Empire
sources.note: Ahuni of Bit Adini surrendered to Shalmaneser in the winter of 857/856. Read for neo-assyrian-empire.

sources.title: Tell Ahmar
sources.note: Til Barsip, capital of Bit Adini, 20 km south of Carchemish; conquered by Assyria in 856 BC and renamed Kar-Shulmanu-asharedu.

notes:
SCOPE. One of the Aramean states of the Jazira the brief names; Cliopatria lacks it (cliopatria_names empty). The Aramean states Bit Bahiani (own dossier) and Carchemish, Bit Agusi (Arpad), Aram-Damascus, Hama and Bit-Zamani/Bit-Halupe have no dossier or only a mention.
PAGES. Three (Bit Adini, Tell Ahmar, Neo-Assyrian Empire shared). The Shalmaneser III page was opened and has nothing on Bit Adini (only Carchemish tribute, Damascus 841, Babylon 851, the Chaldeans from the 850s, Qarqar 853).
DISAGREEMENTS. The Bit Adini page ends the kingdom 856-5 but has Ahuni join the Qarqar coalition in 853 and "submitted and gave tribute" (undated): not used as a vassal tie (the neo-assyrian-empire ledger has no vassal_start). In 883 "a figure from Bit Adini was brought in to rule the Assyrian province of Bit-Halupe" (Ashurnasirpal II); not an event here. Adad-nirari II (911-891) received a "large female monkey and small female monkey" as a gift (undated, not tribute).
REGION. 38.1 E 36.7 N km 70 is the neo-assyrian-empire dossier's circle for the same gain. Gazetteer names missing: Bit Adini, Til Barsip (Tell Ahmar), Carchemish, Masuwari, Asmu, Dabigu, Dummetu, Kaprabu, La'la'ru.
